questions.question: Which statements about hybrid search in RAG are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It combines lexical (keyword) and semantic (vector) retrieval
Disabling vector search and using keywords only
It can improve recall for rare terms or exact matches
It works only when the query contains no keywords

questions.explanation: Hybrid search combines keyword matching with vector similarity. Keyword retrieval helps with exact terms, while vector retrieval finds semantic matches.

questions.question: Which statements about normalizing embedding vectors are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Normalization can make similarity comparisons more consistent
Normalizing changes the number of dimensions
Normalizing scales a vector to unit length
With unit vectors, cosine similarity aligns with the dot product

questions.explanation: Normalization removes magnitude as a factor and preserves direction. Unit vectors have magnitude 1, so cosine similarity equals their dot product.

questions.question: Which of the following are commonly cited examples of small/efficient language models? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Any model exceeding 100B parameters by definition

questions.explanation: Gemma small variants, Phi family models, and smaller Llama variants are widely cited efficient language models. Models above 100B parameters are not small by definition.
